tools.name: agent_review_submit
tools.description: Submit the review of a pull request of a card. Only a running review worker of the card can call it: the call must come from the loupe CLI session of a worker run with the code-review role on this card. Pass the cardId, the URL of a pull request that the card links, the full 40-character commit SHA that you reviewed, a summary, and the findings. Each finding names a file path relative to the repository root, a line range on the reviewed commit, a severity (important, nit or pre-existing), a title and a body. A finding has a category: code (the default) or spec, a gap between the change and the approved design. Only a spec finding can leave out the path and the lines, for a requirement that no code builds. A spec finding can also set needsPerson, for a gap that a worker cannot settle from the design and the code alone. Loupe stores the review against that commit, also when the pull request has a newer head. The result field current says whether the commit matches the last head commit that Loupe read from the forge. That commit can be older than the head on the forge. The review fails when a finding has a severity that the project counts as failing, important by default.

cardId.description: the id of the card under review

pullRequestUrl.description: the URL of a pull request that the card links

headSha.description: the full SHA of the commit you reviewed, 40 lowercase hex characters

summary.description: a short summary of the review

findings.description: the findings, an empty list when the review found nothing

path.description: the file path relative to the repository root, required unless category is spec

startLine.description: the first line of the range, on the reviewed commit, required with a path

endLine.description: the last line of the range, the same as startLine for one line, required with a path

category.description: code for a defect of the code, spec for a gap between the change and the approved design, code when left out

needsPerson.description: true on a spec finding that a worker cannot settle from the design and the code alone, because the design is unclear, contradicts itself or looks wrong against the code, or the change departs from it on purpose with no departure on file. Leave it out for a finding where the code simply does not build what the design says. Only a spec finding can set it

title.description: one line that names the problem

body.description: what is wrong and how to fix it

tools.name: analysis_get
tools.description: Read one analysis of this project. Pass analysisId, the subject id of your analysis work request. The response has id, topic (cost, time, experiment, host or question), scope with range (thirty-days, ninety-days or all: the runs the analysis reads) and, for the experiment topic, experiment (the name of the experiment it compares, to pass to experiment_get), question (null unless the topic is question), model, effort, state (waiting, running, done, failed or paused), reason (why it failed or paused, else null), createdAt, finishedAt, documentId (the report document once done, else null), costUsd (the cost in US dollars of the runs of this analysis so far, null when no run has a known cost) and proposals. Each proposal has id, kind (card or bucket-rule), title, body, payload, estimatedSaving, state (proposed, created or dismissed), dismissReason and cardId (the card it created). Read the runs with metric_query, then write the report with document_create and finish with analysis_report.

analysisId.description: the id of the analysis, the subject id of your work request

tools.name: analysis_report
tools.description: Finish an analysis of this project with its report. First write the report with document_create, then pass its id as documentId. Pass analysisId, the subject id of your analysis work request. proposals lists at most 20 changes you propose, in the order the owner reads them, and an empty list is valid. Each proposal has kind, title and body. kind is card for a change that becomes a backlog card when the owner accepts it, or bucket-rule for a rule that groups tool calls into a time bucket. title is one line of at most 200 characters. body is the detail, in Markdown. payload is required for a bucket-rule: an object with pattern, a glob over a tool call signature, and bucket, a name of lower case letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. estimatedSaving is an optional short text of at most 200 characters, such as "about $4 a week". The analysis then reads done, and the owner accepts or dismisses each proposal on the Reports page. A done or failed analysis takes no second report. The response is the analysis, as analysis_get answers it.

analysisId.description: the id of the analysis, the subject id of your work request

documentId.description: the id of the report document, from document_create

payload.description: for a bucket-rule: pattern and bucket

estimatedSaving.description: a short text, such as "about $4 a week"

tools.name: analytics_settings_get
tools.description: Read the analysis settings of this project. defaultModel and defaultEffort are the values the project sets, or null when it sets none. model and effort are the values a new analysis takes when it names none: the project value, else the instance default. effort is low, medium, high, xhigh or max. collectFullText says whether the bridge sends the full text of each tool call. subcommandPrograms is the list of programs whose second word joins the signature of a shell command, such as git or npm, as this project sets it. It is empty when the project sets none, so the instance list applies. Change the settings with analytics_settings_update.

tools.name: analytics_settings_update
tools.description: Change the analysis settings of this project. Pass only the values you change: an argument you leave out keeps its value. defaultModel is the model a new analysis takes when it names none, one word such as sonnet or opus. defaultEffort is low, medium, high, xhigh or max. Pass clearDefaultModel or clearDefaultEffort true to clear the project value, so the instance default applies. An empty string also clears it. collectFullText says whether the bridge sends the full text of each tool call. subcommandPrograms is the list of programs whose second word joins the signature of a shell command, such as git or npm. Pass at most 50 names of letters, digits and . _ + - and pass an empty list to clear the project list, so the instance list applies. The response is the settings, as analytics_settings_get answers them.

defaultModel.description: the model, or an empty string to clear it

clearDefaultModel.description: true clears the project model; do not pass it with defaultModel

defaultEffort.description: low, medium, high, xhigh or max, or an empty string to clear it

clearDefaultEffort.description: true clears the project effort; do not pass it with defaultEffort

collectFullText.description: whether the bridge sends the full text of each tool call

subcommandPrograms.description: the programs whose second word joins a shell signature, or an empty list to clear them

tools.name: artifact_archive
tools.description: Archive a stored design artifact. It disappears from artifact_list unless includeArchived is true, and its versions and files stay readable. Nothing is deleted. Archiving is curation, so use it only when asked. Archiving an archived artifact changes nothing.

artifactId.description: The UUID of the artifact to archive

tools.name: artifact_get
tools.description: Describe one stored design artifact: its name, archive state, source link and every version with its notes on what changed, its file count and size, plus the files of one version (path, content type, size) and pageLink, a full web address that opens the entry page of that version as the app serves it, valid for one hour. Defaults to the latest version. Read a file's content with artifact_read.

artifactId.description: The UUID of the artifact, from artifact_list or card_get

versionNumber.description: The version whose files to list. Defaults to the latest.

tools.name: artifact_list
tools.description: List the stored design artifacts of the token's project, newest first. Each row has its name, its latest version number, its archive state and where it came from. Read an artifact's files with artifact_get, then artifact_read. Archived artifacts are omitted unless includeArchived is true. Paginated: pass page to walk further, and keep going while hasMore is true.

perPage.description: How many artifacts to return per page

includeArchived.description: Include archived artifacts, which are omitted by default

tools.name: artifact_read
tools.description: Read one file of a stored design artifact by its path, from the latest version unless versionNumber is given. A text file (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, SVG, JSON, Markdown) is returned as text. A PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP image is returned as an image. Any other binary file is refused, and the refusal names its size. List the paths with artifact_get.

path.description: The path of the file inside the version, as artifact_get lists it

versionNumber.description: The version to read from. Defaults to the latest.

tools.name: artifact_unarchive
tools.description: Restore an archived design artifact so artifact_list shows it again. Restoring a live artifact changes nothing.

artifactId.description: The UUID of the artifact to unarchive

tools.name: automation_settings_update
tools.description: Turn the workflow of the project board on or off, the same switch as the Automation page of the project settings. While it is off, the workflow moves no card and asks for no work. stuckDelayMinutes is the minutes a pull request may wait for a merge or for any card change before its card shows Stuck. approvalCoversConflictResolution says whether an approval of a pull request still covers a merge from the base that holds a conflict resolution. It is true by default. Set it to false and the pull request waits for a new approval after such a merge. The value belongs to the copy of the workflow template that this project holds. A setting you leave out keeps the value it has. The result gives the value of every setting after the change.

enabled.description: whether the workflow of the board moves the cards and asks for their work

stuckDelayMinutes.description: the minutes a pull request may wait for a merge or for any card change before its card shows Stuck, from 1 to 1440

approvalCoversConflictResolution.description: whether an approval still covers a merge from the base that holds a conflict resolution

tools.name: board_columns
tools.description: List the columns of the project board, in board order. Each board has its own columns, so read them here before you pass a status to card_create, card_update or card_list. Each column has a slug, a label, a terminal flag, a default flag and a backlog flag. The slug is the value you pass as status. The label is the name a person sees on the board. A terminal column is where finished work goes: a card that enters one gets a completion time. The row with backlog true is Backlog, slug backlog, where a new card lands when you pass no status. Its default flag is also true. The board does not draw Backlog as a column, and nobody can rename, reorder or delete it. Renaming a column changes its slug. The response also lists the card types of the project in types, and the type a new card gets in defaultType. Each type has a key, a label, and the capabilities children and lane. The key is the value you pass as type to card_create, card_update and card_list, and a key the project does not declare is refused. A card of a type with children true may be the parent of other cards. A card of a type with lane true gets a lane on the board.

tools.name: bridge_command_cancel
tools.description: Withdraw the resume or stop command that waits on a worker run, before its bridge reads it. Pass runId, from worker_run_list. results has one row. A row with outcome cancelled carries commandId, the id of the withdrawn command. A row with outcome refused carries code and message. The codes are: not-found (no run of this project has this id) and nothing-pending (no command waits on the run, or its bridge already read it).

runId.description: the id of the worker run whose command to withdraw, from worker_run_list

tools.name: bridge_host_samples
tools.description: List the host samples of the bridge that ran one worker run, oldest first. A host sample is one reading of the machine the bridge runs on. The samples cover the time from the start of the run to its end, or to now while the run is open. They describe the whole machine, so they cover every run on that bridge in that window, not only this run. A bridge sends samples only when the instance flag bridge.host_sampling_enabled is on and the rules.yaml of the bridge does not set collect: false, so a run can have none. Each sample has sampledAt, cpuPct (the use of each core, in percent), meanCpuPct (the mean of cpuPct, rounded to one decimal, or null when cpuPct is empty), memUsed, memTotal and swapUsed (in bytes), batteryPct (null on a machine with no battery) and onAc (whether the machine runs on mains power, or null when it does not say). The response also has runId, bridgeId, and note, which says why the list is empty when the run has no bridge or no start, and is null otherwise. The response is paginated: pass page to walk further, and keep going while hasMore is true. perPage defaults to 100, with a maximum of 500.

runId.description: the id of a worker run of this project, from worker_run_list

perPage.description: how many samples to return per page

tools.name: bridge_list
tools.description: List the CLI bridges that follow this project. A bridge runs the workers of the project on a machine. Each bridge has bridgeId, name, requestedName, gitIdentity, liveness, quietCause, lastSeenAt, cliVersion, pauseRequested, pausedReported, takesCommands, takesReruns, acceptsEntries, commandEntries, workerPools, workerPoolsReportedAt, accounts, accountsReportedAt and openRuns. name is the name the bridge holds, or null. requestedName is the name its last heartbeat asked for, or null. A requestedName with a null name means another bridge of the owner already holds that name. gitIdentity is the git identity of the bridge for this project, or null when it reported none. It has mode, commitName, pushLogin and githubUserId. mode is agent_account, app_token or machine. pushLogin is the GitHub login the pushes use, or empty when it is unknown. githubUserId is the numeric id of that login, or null. liveness is live while the bridge sends its heartbeat, and quiet when it missed several. quietCause is null for a live bridge, login-expired when a quiet bridge lost the login that can no longer refresh, and unknown for any other quiet bridge. lastSeenAt is the time of its last heartbeat. pauseRequested says that a person asked the bridge to start no new work. pausedReported says whether the bridge reported that it is paused, or is null when it reported nothing. takesCommands is false for an older bridge, which cannot resume or stop a run. takesReruns is false for a bridge that cannot run a failed command run again. acceptsEntries is true when the bridge adds a proposed command entry to its rule file after the owner confirms. commandEntries lists each command entry the bridge can run, with name, description, params, run and timeout, as its last heartbeat reported them, or is null. Each param has name, pattern and description, and a value must match its pattern whole. run is the argv with its placeholders. workerPools lists each pool of the bridge with its name, size, inUse and queued counts, as its last heartbeat reported them, or is null. accounts lists each account the bridge checked with name, harness, state ready or failing, reason, and used, as its last heartbeat reported them, or is null. used is false for an account that no rule uses, which turns off no rule when it fails. accountsReportedAt is the time of the heartbeat that carried the accounts. openRuns lists the queued, resumed, preparing, running and stopping runs of this project on the bridge, each with runId, subjectType, subjectId, cardNumber, workKind and state. subjectType names what the run is about, such as card, and subjectId is its id. cardNumber is null when the subject is no card. workKind is the kind of the work request the run ran, or null.

tools.name: bucket_rule_create
tools.description: Add a time bucket rule to the end of the rules of this project. pattern is a glob of at most 120 characters, where * matches any run of characters and ? matches one, such as LSP or mcp__loupe__*. bucket is the bucket name, 1 to 64 characters: lower case letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. A project holds at most 50 rules. The rule applies to the tool calls of every run, and the bucket times of the project are computed again. The response is the rules, as bucket_rule_list answers them.

tools.name: bucket_rule_delete
tools.description: Delete a time bucket rule, by its id from bucket_rule_list. The tool calls it matched fall to a later rule or to the other bucket, and the bucket times of the project are computed again. The response is the rules that remain, as bucket_rule_list answers them.

ruleId.description: the id of the rule, from bucket_rule_list

tools.name: bucket_rule_list
tools.description: List the time bucket rules of this project, in the order they apply. A tool call takes the bucket of the first rule whose pattern matches it. Each rule gives its id, its position, its pattern and its bucket. The pattern is a glob of at most 120 characters, where * matches any run of characters and ? matches one. limit is the most rules a project holds. Change the rules with bucket_rule_create, bucket_rule_move and bucket_rule_delete.

tools.name: bucket_rule_move
tools.description: Move a time bucket rule one place up or down, by its id from bucket_rule_list. A tool call takes the bucket of the first rule that matches it, so the order decides. direction is up or down. The first rule cannot move up and the last cannot move down, so those moves change nothing. The bucket times of the project are computed again. The response is the rules, as bucket_rule_list answers them.

ruleId.description: the id of the rule, from bucket_rule_list

tools.name: card_create
tools.description: Add a card to the project board. Give it a title, a Markdown body and a type. board_columns lists the types this project declares, with the capabilities of each, and a type it does not declare is refused. A type with the children capability groups the child cards that together build one feature. Pass parentCardId to put the new card under a card of such a type in this project. Only a card of a type with the children capability can be a parent, and such a card cannot have a parent. laneEnabled says whether the board draws a lane for a card of a type with the lane capability, and it defaults to true. With no status, the card lands in Backlog, whose slug is backlog. The board does not draw Backlog as a column, and Backlog has its own page. To place the card elsewhere, pass status, the slug of a column. Each board has its own columns, and board_columns lists them. A terminal column is where finished work goes, and a card created in one gets a completion time. Pass pullRequestUrls to link the pull requests that carry the work; a URL from an unrecognised forge is kept as given rather than rejected. Pass documentIds to link the documents the work is written up in; unlike a pull request URL, an id naming no document of this project is refused rather than kept. artifactIds works the same way for the artifacts of this project. The card records reporter agent unless you pass human, which says a person raised it and you are only writing it down. Passing reviewer is refused: the live-review widget writes that value, and it means somebody the app could not name raised the card. Pass relatedCards to link other cards of this project. Each entry takes a cardId and a kind: relates-to (the default), blocks, blocked-by, has-follow-up or follow-up-of. A follow-up is a card with no parent that waits for the card it follows; follow-up-of names the followed card, and has-follow-up names the follow-up. A link to the card itself, to a card outside this project, or to one card twice is refused. childDesign says whether the tech design of the parent covers the card, for a card under a parent whose tech design is approved. Pass inherit to link that design: choose it for a fix inside a decision the design already made, and the card starts with the other children. Pass own for a card that asks an open question or changes a decision of the design: the card goes to Tech design and gets a design of its own, so pass no status with it. Without the choice, the owner answers a question about the card. When the owner would get that question, the call is refused until you pass the choice. requiresHumanReview says whether a person must review the pull request of the card: true when a person must review it, and a new card has it off unless you pass true. A new card has no switch to lower, so a bridge worker may pass either value. The response carries a number, the short label that counts from 1 inside this project. Say "card 42" and name a branch after it. It is not the cardId, and another project has its own card 42. card_get and card_update accept it, so use the cardId or the number to read or change it. In the body, write another card as card:<number> and a pull request as pr:owner/repo#<number>; Loupe turns each into a link with a title tooltip. A title shows a token as plain text.

body.description: what the card asks for, in Markdown

status.description: the slug of the column the card lands in, from board_columns; defaults to backlog

reporter.description: who raised the card, agent or human; defaults to agent

pullRequestUrls.description: pull request URLs to link to the card

documentIds.description: ids of documents in this project to link; any other id is refused

artifactIds.description: ids of artifacts in this project to link; any other id is refused

relatedCards.description: cards of this project to link, each with a cardId and a kind

cardId.description: the id of a card of this project

kind.description: how this card reads the other card

parentCardId.description: the id of a card of this project, of a type with the children capability, that the card belongs to; omit it for no parent

laneEnabled.description: whether the board draws a lane for this card, when its type has the lane capability; defaults to true

childDesign.description: inherit or own, for a card under a parent whose tech design is approved; inherit links that design, and own moves the card to Tech design

requiresHumanReview.description: true when a person must review the pull request; a bridge worker can only turn it on; defaults to false

tools.name: card_get
tools.description: Read one card from the project board, with its full Markdown body and every pull request linked to it. Each pull request carries state, the last state Loupe read from the forge: state, draft, checks, failedChecks, mergeability, review, readyToMerge and refreshedAt. state is null when Loupe holds no reading, such as for a link it cannot parse or a pull request it has not read yet. siteReviewComments lists the feedback items that belong to the card, each with its id, url, surface (web or ios-simulator), native (what a native note says about the app, device, screen and element, or null), screenshot (the width and height of the marked image of the note, or null), anchors, body, hasDrawing, status, context and createdAt; mark one addressed with feedback_mark_addressed. The answer carries the screenshots of the pending notes as images after the JSON, newest note first, at most ten. imagesOmitted counts the pending screenshots left out; read them with feedback_list, passing the cardId of this card and imageOffset 10. relatedCards lists the linked cards, each with its cardId, number, title, status and kind as this card reads it: a blocks link from card A reads blocked-by from card B, and a has-follow-up link from card A reads follow-up-of from card B. parent names the card the card belongs to, or null. A card whose type has the children capability lists its children, and progress counts how many of them sit in a terminal column (done) out of all of them (total); progress is null for a type without that capability. laneEnabled says whether the board draws a lane for an epic. requiresHumanReview is true when a person must review the pull request of the card. pause is null, or names the active workflow pause that holds the card: pauseId, kind (rule, retries, work-limit, work-timeout or work-stopped), reason, ruleId and since. state is null, or what the card needs now on the board: kind (stuck, needs-you, working or waiting), code (why), since (when that reason began, or null when Loupe stores none), reason (one sentence that says why) and others (the other reasons that apply, each with kind, code, reason and since). A card in a terminal column has no state. Use a card id from card_list or card_create. The response also carries a number, the short label that counts from 1 inside this project. Use the number to name the card to a person. Pass the cardId or the number to read a card, never both.

cardId.description: the id of the card to read, from card_list or card_create; pass it or number, never both

number.description:
the card number, the short label that counts from 1 inside this project; pass it instead of cardId

The card is the structured result, and the images of its pending notes follow its JSON

tools.name: card_get_history
tools.description: Read the history of one card, newest first: when it was created, each move between columns with who made it and why, and each action the board automation took on it. The response is paginated: pass page to walk further, and keep going while hasMore is true. perPage defaults to 50, with a maximum of 100. Each event carries kind (created, moved, fix-requested, stopped, ready-to-merge, synced, run-finished, paused, pause-released, verdict, review-overridden, override-ended, document-verdict, verdict-failed, auto-approved, approval-dismissed, human-review-changed or value-changed), occurredAt, and actor with its kind (human, agent, reviewer or system) and the name of the person behind it, or null. from and to name a column by id, slug and label: a move sets both, a creation sets to alone, and every other kind sets neither. cause says why the app moved the card on its own, such as a merged pull request, or is null. pullRequest comes from an automation action or an agent review override entry, reason from a fix-requested or stopped one on a pull request, or the reason code of a pause, and neither from a stopped event of a run that a workflow rule stopped, and run holds the whole record of a finished run. pause holds the kind of the pause (rule, retries, work-limit, work-timeout or work-stopped) and the ruleId that set it, on a paused or pause-released event only. On a pause-released event, pause also holds releaseReason, the code that says why the pause ended, such as facts-changed or released-by-person. releaseReason is null on a paused event and on an older event. override holds the approver and the headSha of the pull request head on a review-overridden event, and the headSha on an override-ended event; approver is null there. document holds documentId, title, rule, verdict, withdrawn and refusal, on a document-verdict or verdict-failed event only. A document-verdict event is a verdict on a design document of the card: verdict is approved, changes-requested or withdrawn, rule names the workflow rule that wrote it or is null for a person, and withdrawn names the verdict that a withdrawal took back. A verdict-failed event means a rule tried to approve a document and the app refused: refusal is a short code such as verdict_stale, and the other keys of document are null. humanReview holds value, cause and ruleId, on a human-review-changed event only: value is true when the switch went on, cause is person, agent, rule or rollout, and ruleId names the workflow rule that set it, or is null. valueChange holds key, value and previous, on a value-changed event only: it is the key of the card value that changed, the new value, and the value before, which is null when the key was unset. The app writes paused, and a person or the app writes pause-released. The history starts empty, so a change made before it began has no event. Pass the cardId or the number to name the card, never both.

cardId.description: the id of the card to read, from card_list or card_create; pass it or number, never both

number.description: the card number, the short label that counts from 1 inside this project; pass it instead of cardId

perPage.description: how many events to return per page

tools.name: card_hold
tools.description: Make a card unmanaged. While the card is unmanaged, the workflow makes no move and starts no work on it, no bridge starts a worker on it, and a person may move it to any column. The hold cancels the work requests of the card that no bridge took yet. This stops no live run, so call worker_run_stop to stop one. A queued run waits, and starts when the card is managed again. The card is managed again on card_release, or when the card is deleted. While the workflow engine is off, a move by a person to another column also makes the card managed again. Pass one of cardId or number to name the card, never both. The result has cardId and outcome. Outcome held means that the card is now unmanaged. A result with outcome refused also carries code and message. The codes are: not-found (this project has no such card, and cardId is null when number names no card), already-paused and card-gone (the card was deleted during the call).

cardId.description: the id of the card; pass it or number, never both

number.description: the card number, the short label that counts from 1 inside this project; pass it instead of cardId

tools.name: card_list
tools.description: List the cards on the project board. Filter by status, the slug of a column on this board. Each board has its own columns. The response lists them in columns, and board_columns lists them alone. You can also filter by type, a key that board_columns lists, by reporter (human, agent, reviewer), who raised the card, or by parentCardId, which reads the children of one card. Pass paused true to read only the cards that a workflow pause holds, or false to read only the cards with none; total and paging count the filtered set. A card is never raised by system, which names the app acting on an approval. An open column reads in board order, by position. A terminal column is where finished work goes, and it reads newest completion first, with no time window on it. Each row is a summary: cardId, number, title, type, status, reporter, parentCardId, updatedAt and state. state is null, or holds kind (stuck, needs-you, working or waiting), code and since: what the card needs now on the board. Each entry of columns has slug, label, terminal and default. Pass full to get the body, the pull request and document links, the feedback items (siteReviewComments), the linked cards (relatedCards), the parent, the lane setting, requiresHumanReview (true when a person must review the pull request), the children and the progress of a card whose type may have children, and the active pause as well, which is far larger. pause is null, or holds pauseId, kind (rule, retries, work-limit, work-timeout or work-stopped), reason, ruleId and since. With full, each pull request also carries its stored state, and state also holds reason and others, as card_get describes. Paginated: pass page to walk further, and keep going while hasMore is true. Every card carries a number, the short label that counts from 1 inside this project. Use it to name a card to a person, and use the cardId or the number to read or change it.

status.description: only cards in the column with this slug; board_columns lists the slugs of this board

type.description: only cards of this type key; board_columns lists the types of this project

reporter.description: only cards raised by this reporter: human, agent or reviewer

perPage.description: how many cards to return per page

full.description: return the whole card, body and links included, rather than the summary

parentCardId.description: only the children of this card of the project

paused.description: true for only the cards with an active pause, false for only those with none

tools.name: card_pause_release
tools.description: Lift the workflow pause of a card, so the paused rule runs again with a fresh budget. The workflow pauses a card when a rule used up its retries (kind retries) or its work limit (kind work-limit), when no bridge took its work in time (kind work-timeout), or when a worker stopped with a refusal that the workflow does not retry (kind work-stopped). Lift a pause only when its cause is gone, for example after an outage. A pause of kind rule ends only on its own release condition, so it is refused. This tool differs from card_release, which makes a card managed again after card_hold. card_get shows the pause of a card in its pause field, and card_list with paused true lists the paused cards. Pass one of cardId or number to name the card, never both. Pass pauseId to lift that pause only, so a pause that changed since you read it is refused. The result has cardId and outcome. Outcome released also carries the kind, reason and ruleId of the pause that ended. A result with outcome refused also carries code and message. The codes are: not-found (this project has no such card, and cardId is null when number names no card), card-unmanaged (the card is unmanaged, or the workflow is off for the project), not-paused, pause-changed (the active pause is not pauseId) and kind-not-releasable.

A rule does not open a second work request while its request is live, and an open work request gets a new timeout. A paused card stays paused, because this tool does not lift a workflow pause, which the workflow makes when a rule runs out of retries or work budget. Call card_pause_release for that. Pass one of cardId or number to name the card, never both. The result has cardId and outcome. Outcome released means that the card is managed again. A result with outcome refused also carries code and message. The codes are: not-found (this project has no such card, and cardId is null when number names no card) and not-paused.

Pass your sessionId, the first set value of $LOUPE_SESSION_ID, $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and $CODEX_THREAD_ID. Pass the skill name as name, for example loupe:product-design. Pass one of cardId or number to name the card, never both. status is optional, and takes the slug of a column on this board. It moves the card in the same step, and this move keeps the run open. Every later move of the card to another column closes the run. A move inside the same column closes nothing. Call card_run_close when the session ends. A second call for the same session and card that does not move the card returns the run that is already open. A second call whose status moves the card to another column closes that run and opens a new one. On a board with the Lifecycle template, pass the Implementation slug as status when you do the work yourself, and the card moves there with no worker. tools.name: card_search
tools.description: Search the project board by words. Use it to answer "is there already a card about this?" before you write a new one. It reads both the title and the body of every card, in every column, terminal columns of finished work included: a topic is often named only in a body, and "yes, and it is already done" is a true answer. Matching is by substring, ignoring case: "pag" finds "paging" and "pages". Punctuation separates words, and every word must match. Quote a phrase to require it, prefix a word or a phrase with - to exclude it, and write or between two terms for either. A number such as 12 or #12 also finds the card with that number. Rows with every word in the title come first, newest first in each group. Each row is a summary: cardId, number, title, type, status, reporter, parentCardId, updatedAt and state, as card_list describes. Call card_get with a cardId to read a body. Paginated: pass page to walk further, and keep going while hasMore is true.

perPage.description: how many cards to return per page

tools.name: card_update
tools.description: Change a card on the project board. Pass one of cardId or number to name the card. Every other field is optional, and a field you leave out keeps the value it has. status takes the slug of a column on this board. backlog is a status that always exists. The board does not draw Backlog as a column, and Backlog has its own page. Each board has its own columns, and board_columns lists them. A terminal column is where finished work goes. Moving a card to a terminal column stamps its completion time; moving it back to a column that is not terminal clears that stamp. A change of status appends the card to the end of the column it arrives in. pullRequestUrls, documentIds and artifactIds are the fields where leaving one out and sending an empty list differ: leave one out and those links stay, send an empty list and every link of that kind is removed. A documentId naming no document of this project is refused, and so is an artifactId naming no artifact of this project. relatedCards works the same way, and it replaces every link that touches the card, including links written from the other card. Send the whole set: the relatedCards of card_get goes back unchanged. Each entry takes a cardId and a kind (relates-to, blocks, blocked-by, has-follow-up or follow-up-of; a follow-up is a card with no parent that waits for the card it follows). type takes a type key from board_columns, and a type the project does not declare is refused. parentCardId puts the card under a card of this project: omit it to keep the parent, pass clearParent true to clear it (an empty string also clears it), or send the id of the new parent. Only a card of a type with the children capability can be a parent, such a card cannot have a parent, and it keeps its type while it has children. laneEnabled says whether the board draws a lane for a card of a type with the lane capability. Reporter cannot be changed, because it records who first raised the card. To finish a card, move it to a terminal column rather than asking for it to be deleted. childDesign says whether the tech design of the parent covers the card, for a card under a parent whose tech design is approved. Pass inherit to link that design: choose it for a fix inside a decision the design already made. Pass own for a card that asks an open question or changes a decision of the design: the card goes to Tech design, so pass no status with it. When the call sets parentCardId and the owner would get a question about the card, the call is refused until you pass the choice. The card number does not change, and you cannot set it. It is the short label that counts from 1 inside this project. requiresHumanReview says whether a person must review the pull request of the card: pass true to require it, and omit it to keep the setting. A bridge worker can only turn it on, and a call from a worker that passes false for a card with the switch on is refused. The card keeps its other fields when the call is refused. This tool takes the cardId or the number, never both. In the body, write another card as card:<number> and a pull request as pr:owner/repo#<number>; Loupe turns each into a link with a title tooltip. A title shows a token as plain text. values sets the typed values of the card, as an object that maps a key to its value, such as {"tech-design-interactive": true}. The workflow template of the project declares the keys and their types, and card_get lists the declared keys of a card in its values. Any caller may write a value, including a bridge worker. A key you leave out keeps its value. A key the template does not declare is refused, and so is a value of the wrong type. One bad entry refuses the whole call and changes nothing, and the error lists the declared keys.

cardId.description: the id of the card to change, from card_list or card_create; pass it or number, never both

number.description: the card number, the short label that counts from 1 inside this project; pass it instead of cardId

body.description: a new Markdown body, replacing the old one

type.description: a new type key; board_columns lists the types this project declares

status.description: the slug of a new column on this board; board_columns lists the slugs

pullRequestUrls.description: the full set of pull request URLs the card carries; omit to keep the current links, send an empty list to remove them all

documentIds.description: the full set of document ids the card carries; omit to keep the current links, send an empty list to remove them all

artifactIds.description: the full set of artifact ids the card carries; omit to keep the current links, send an empty list to remove them all

relatedCards.description: the full set of card links; omit to keep them, send an empty list to remove them all

cardId.description: the id of a card of this project

kind.description: how this card reads the other card

parentCardId.description: the id of a card of this project whose type has the children capability; omit to keep the parent, pass clearParent to clear it

clearParent.description: true removes the card from its parent; do not pass it with parentCardId

laneEnabled.description: whether the board draws a lane for this card, when its type has the lane capability; omit to keep the setting

childDesign.description: inherit or own, for a card under a parent whose tech design is approved; inherit links that design, and own moves the card to Tech design

requiresHumanReview.description: true when a person must review the pull request; a bridge worker can only turn it on; omit to keep the setting

values.description: an object that maps a declared key to its value; card_get lists the declared keys in values; omit to keep every value

The slug is the value you pass as status to the card tools. To make the column terminal, call column_update after this. The result names the slug of the new column and lists every column of the board.

tools.name: document_create

Pass series with seriesOrdinal to say this document is a numbered item of an ordered set, such as post 5 of a blog series. Pass language to record the language the document is written in, when it is not the project's default: one of the PostgreSQL text-search configuration names, such as english, french, german, spanish, portuguese, russian, or simple for text of mixed or unknown language. document_get returns it. Search matches substrings, so the language does not change what finds the document. Pass draft true to keep the document out of review and the reviewer's inbox: a revise keeps it a draft, and document_publish sends it to review. Tags are lowercased. A series name is stored as you spell it and matched ignoring case. Both are created on first use, so read tag_list and series_list first and reuse the project's existing names. In the Markdown, write a card as card:<number> and a pull request as pr:owner/repo#<number>; Loupe turns each into a link with a title tooltip. A token inside code, a link or square brackets stays as written.

markdown.description: The document content in Markdown format

description.description: What this first version is, in one or two sentences — the brief it answers or the question it exists to settle

tags.description: Tag names to group this document by, lowercased on write and created if the project does not have them yet

references.description: Ids of documents in the same project that this one points at; the link is shown on both documents

draft.description: Create the document as a draft: it stays out of review and the inbox, and a revise keeps it a draft, until document_publish sends it to review

Never answer on your own judgement. Pass versionNumber, the version you showed the owner. A newer version is refused. Pass optionIndexes, the indexes of the options the owner chose, counting from 0. Leave note out to keep the note that the owner wrote. Pass an empty note to remove it. The review page shows that an agent recorded the answer. A bridge worker is refused. The response says whether the answer changed.

versionNumber.description: the version you showed the owner

decisionId.description: the id of the decision block

optionIndexes.description: the indexes of the options the owner chose, counting from 0

note.description: the note of the owner; leave it out to keep the stored note, pass an empty string to remove it

tools.description: Clear the chosen options of a decision block of a document, for the owner's account. Call it only after the owner asked for it in the chat. Never clear an answer on your own judgement. Pass versionNumber, the version you showed the owner. A newer version is refused. The note that the owner wrote stays. A bridge worker is refused. The response says whether the answer changed.

versionNumber.description: the version you showed the owner

decisionId.description: the id of the decision block

tools.name: document_get
tools.description: Fetch a document's current Markdown source, title, language, status, archive state and reason, version number, that version's description, its tags, its place in a series, and the documents it references.

documentId.description: The UUID of the document to retrieve

tools.name: document_get_review
tools.description: Fetch the review state (verdict, status, threaded comments, answered decision blocks, and the agent reviews with their answers) for a document's current version. Every comment and reply reports whether an agent or a human wrote it, and a comment may carry a replacement for the text it quotes. A decision block reports its type: a single-choice block answers in selected, and a multiple-choice block answers in selections. verdictId is the id of the newest entry of the verdict log, a withdrawal included, and verdictThroughAgent says that an agent recorded it for the owner. The verdict tools take that verdictId. Each decision reports through_agent when an agent recorded its answer for the owner.

documentId.description:
the UUID of the document whose review to retrieve

`verdict` is null when no review has been submitted for the current version yet

A comment's `status` is one of pending, addressed or resolved and belongs to the whole
thread, so only the root comment reports it

Each `id` is the value document_reply_to_comment and document_mark_comment_addressed take

`author` is agent or human — the class of writer, not an identity, so no name or address
of a human reviewer is reported

`replacement` is what the reviewer wants the quoted passage to become: null means they
proposed no edit, an empty string means delete the passage, and any other value is the
text to put in its place. Only root comments carry it. Loupe never edits the document —
applying these is your job: rewrite the markdown and call document_revise. On a comment
with a replacement the `quote` is the verbatim selected span, so it can be substituted
as-is; on every other comment it is widened to whole words for readability and must not
be used for a find-and-replace

An `orphaned: true` comment's quote no longer appears in the document, so its replacement
has no target and cannot be applied — reply to it instead of guessing

`decisions` lists every decision block in the current version. `selected` is null while a
decision is unanswered, and otherwise the option as it read when the reviewer chose it

`selected_index` points into the same entry's `options`, and is null when the chosen option
is no longer among them — `answered_at_version` then says which version it came from

`type` is single or multiple. A multiple-choice block takes any number of answers, so it
reports null in `selected`, `selected_index`, `answered_at` and `answered_at_version`

`selections` lists every recorded answer of either kind of block, each with the `option`
text, its `index` in `options`, and when and against which version it was chosen. Read it
for a multiple-choice block, and read it for a single-choice one too if you want one shape

`note` is the text the reviewer wrote beside their choice, or null when they wrote none.
`updated_at` is when the answer was last saved, and is null for an unanswered decision.
A decision can carry a note with no option chosen, so read the note even when `selections`
is empty

Each decision's `id` is the one the document declared in its fence, and it is permanent:
changing it in a revision discards the answer keyed to the old one

`through_agent` is true when an agent recorded the answer for the owner, and false otherwise

`verdictId` is the id of the newest entry of the verdict log on the current version, a
withdrawal included, or null while the log is empty. The verdict tools take it, so read
it again before you call one. `verdictThroughAgent` is true when an agent recorded that
entry for the owner, and false when the log is empty

`agentReviews` lists each agent review of the document, newest first. Each carries the
`cardId` of the card it reviewed, the `versionNumber` that the reviewer read, its
`conclusion`, its `findings` with their `index`, and the `answer` of the fix round to
each finding, or null before it answers.
`answered` says whether the fix round has answered the review

tools.name: document_list
tools.description: List documents in the token's project, with their current status and version. Each row carries that version's description, which says what the document is about, so you rarely need document_get to find the one you want. Each row also carries its tags and, when it has one, its series and position in it. Narrow the list with search, which matches text anywhere inside a word, and with status, tag and series. A search puts the documents with every word in the title first, and a series orders them by position. Archived documents are omitted unless includeArchived is true. Paginated: pass page to walk further, and keep going while hasMore is true.

perPage.description: How many documents to return per page

includeArchived.description: Include archived documents, which are omitted by default

search.description: Terms matched against every document's title and current content, anywhere inside a word and ignoring case. Quotes, a leading minus and or work as in card_search. A document with every word in the title comes first, newest first in each group.

status.description: Keep only documents in this state: in-review, approved, changes-requested or draft

tag.description: Keep only documents carrying this tag; matched ignoring case and surrounding spaces. Read tag_list for the project's vocabulary.

series.description: Keep only documents in this series, matched ignoring case, and order them by their position in it. Read series_list for the project's names.

tools.name: document_mark_comment_addressed
tools.description: Mark document-review comment threads as addressed after acting on them. Accepts the root comment ids returned by document_get_review, and only ids from the document's current version — revising a document mints new comment rows, so re-read the review after document_revise. Ids that are unknown, superseded by a newer version, already addressed, already resolved, or point at a reply rather than a thread root are skipped, not fatal.

tools.name: document_publish
tools.description: Send a draft document to review, so it reaches the reviewer's inbox. A document that is not a draft is returned unchanged, with published false. An archived document is refused. No new version is created.

documentId.description: The UUID of the draft document to send to review

tools.name: document_rename
tools.description: Change a document's title without creating a new version. Renames one document per call.

documentId.description: The UUID of the document to rename

tools.name: document_reply_to_comment
tools.description: Reply to a document-review comment. Takes a comment id from document_get_review, and only an id from the document's current version — revising a document mints new comment rows, so reply before calling document_revise, or re-read the review after it. The reply is attributed to the agent, not to the document owner. Replying to a reply is rejected: reply to the thread root instead.

commentId.description: the id of the comment to reply to, from document_get_review

tools.name: document_review_answer
tools.description: Answer each finding of the latest agent review that a card got for a draft design document. A review of another card that links the same document does not count. Only a running design fix worker of the card can call it: the call must come from the loupe CLI session of a worker run with the design-revise role on this card. Pass the cardId, the documentId and one answer for each finding of the latest review, counted from 0 in the order document_get_review lists them. An answer is fixed, not-changed with a reason, or to-owner for a finding that only the owner can settle. A finding that needs a person always takes to-owner. Call it once, after you revise the draft. A review that already has its answers refuses a second call.

cardId.description: the id of the card that the document belongs to

documentId.description: the id of the draft document that you revised

answers.description: one answer for each finding of the latest review, an empty list when it had none

index.description: the position of the finding in the latest review, counted from 0

reason.description: why the finding stays as it is, required with not-changed, and optional with the other answers

tools.name: document_review_submit
tools.description: Submit the review of a draft design document of a card. Only a running design review worker of the card can call it: the call must come from the loupe CLI session of a worker run with the design-review role on this card. Pass the cardId, the documentId of a draft that the card links, the versionNumber that you read, a summary, and the findings. Each finding has a severity (important, nit or pre-existing), a title and a body, and names no file. A finding can set needsPerson, for a gap that a worker cannot settle from the design and the code alone and that the owner must decide. The review fails when a finding without needsPerson has a severity that the project counts as failing, important by default.

cardId.description: the id of the card that the document belongs to

documentId.description: the id of the draft document under review

versionNumber.description: the number of the version that you read

summary.description: a short summary of the review

findings.description: the findings, an empty list when the review found nothing

needsPerson.description: true on a finding that a worker cannot settle from the design and the code alone, because the design is unclear, contradicts itself or looks wrong against the code. Leave it out for a finding that the fix worker can fix

title.description: one line that names the problem

body.description: what is wrong and how to fix it

tools.name: document_revise
tools.description: Submit a new Markdown version of a document, described by what changed in it. Open comments are re-anchored onto the new version; those whose quoted text no longer appears are flagged orphaned. Pass title to correct the document title at the same time, and references to replace the documents this one points at. Pass series with seriesOrdinal to move the document to a place in an ordered set, or an empty series to take it out of one. In the Markdown, write a card as card:<number> and a pull request as pr:owner/repo#<number>; Loupe turns each into a link with a title tooltip. A token inside code, a link or square brackets stays as written.

documentId.description: The UUID of the document to revise

markdown.description: The new Markdown content for the document

description.description: What changed in this version and why, in one or two sentences, for a reviewer who read the previous one — name what you rewrote, added or dropped, not that you revised it

title.description: A corrected title for the document; omit to keep the current one

references.description: The complete set of document ids this one points at, replacing the current set; omit to keep it, pass an empty list to clear it

series.description: Name of the ordered set this document belongs to, stored as you spell it and created if the project does not have it yet; omit to leave the placement alone, pass an empty string to take the document out of its series

seriesOrdinal.description: Position of this document in that series, counting from 1; required whenever series is given

tools.name: document_set_references
tools.description: Replace the set of documents a document points at, without creating a new version. Passing an empty list clears them. Targets must be in the same project and a document cannot reference itself; read document_get first, because this replaces the current set rather than adding to it.

documentId.description: The UUID of the document whose references to replace

references.description: The complete set of document ids this one should point at, replacing whatever it points at now; pass an empty list to clear them

tools.name: document_set_series
tools.description: Place a document at a numbered position in an ordered set, such as post 5 of a blog series. Omit both series and seriesOrdinal to take the document out of the series it is in. A series name is stored as you spell it, matched ignoring case, and created on first use. No two documents in one series may hold the same number.

documentId.description: The UUID of the document to place

series.description: Name of the ordered set the document belongs to; omit to take it out of its series

seriesOrdinal.description: Position of the document in that series, counting from 1; required whenever series is given

tools.name: document_set_tags
tools.description: Replace a document's tags with the given set. Passing an empty list clears them. Tags are lowercased and created on first use — read tag_list first so a new name is a deliberate one.

documentId.description: The UUID of the document to tag

tags.description: The complete set of tag names the document should carry, replacing whatever it has now

tools.name: document_unarchive
tools.description: Restore an archived document so it appears in the reviewer's default document list again. No new version is created, and the document's content and status are untouched. Unarchiving a document that is not archived changes nothing.

documentId.description: The UUID of the document to restore

tools.name: document_verdict_submit
tools.description: Record the verdict of the owner on a document, for the owner's account. Call it only after the owner gave the verdict in the chat. Never give a verdict on your own judgement. The verdict is approved or changes-requested. An approval moves the card of the document on. A verdict on a draft stops its agent review. Pass versionNumber, the version you showed the owner. A newer version is refused. Take expectedVerdictId from verdictId in document_get_review. Pass null when verdictId is null. A newer verdict is refused. Approval needs an answer to every decision. Changes-requested needs a note or an open comment. The review page shows that an agent recorded the verdict. A bridge worker is refused.

versionNumber.description: the version you showed the owner

expectedVerdictId.description: the verdictId from document_get_review, or null when that is null

note.description: the note of the owner for the verdict

tools.name: document_verdict_withdraw
tools.description: Withdraw the newest verdict on a document, for the owner's account. Call it only after the owner asked for it in the chat. Never withdraw a verdict on your own judgement. Pass versionNumber, the version you showed the owner. A newer version is refused. Take verdictId from verdictId in document_get_review. A newer verdict is refused. The review page shows that an agent recorded the withdrawal. A bridge worker is refused.

versionNumber.description: the version you showed the owner

tools.name: experiment_archive
tools.description: Archive an experiment of this project. It leaves the main Experiments list and shows under the archived filter, and its page and data stay readable. Pins and variant assignment work as before. A worker run that Loupe first records after the archive brings the experiment back by itself. Archiving is curation, so use it only when asked. An experiment that no run and no pin names is refused. Archiving an archived experiment moves its archive time forward.

experiment.description: the name of the experiment to archive, as worker_run_list and experiment_get name it

tools.name: experiment_get
tools.description: Read the comparison of one experiment of this project, as its Comparison and Cards tabs show it. Pass experiment, the name of the experiment. The response has experiment, archived (true when the owner archived the experiment and no run has brought it back), baseline (the variant that the rule names as the baseline, or null when the experiment names none), confidenceLevel, declaredMetrics (the metric keys the rule declares, in their order, or null when it declares none and the default metrics apply), unknownMetrics (the declared keys that no metric has), unknownGuards (the guard keys that no metric has, which the headline leaves out), minFinishedCards, headline, variants, metrics, includedCards, leftOutCards and cards. confidenceLevel is the level of every range in the answer: 0.95 for one comparison or none, and 1 - 0.05 / N for N comparisons, so 0.975 for two. A money value is in US dollars, a duration of a built-in metric in milliseconds, a duration of a metric that the workflow template declares in hours, and a ratio is between 0 and 1. Every variant is compared against the baseline, never against another variant. headline has goal, baselineArm, comparisons, guards and controls. goal is what the experiment tries to improve, with key, label and valueType of its metric (valueType is null for an unknown-metric goal), direction (lower or higher, the better way, or null when the rule names none) and problem. problem is unknown-metric when the rule names a goal key that no metric has, no-direction when the rule names a goal with no better way, else null. With a problem there is no comparison. baselineArm is the baseline with name, point and cardsBehind, or null with no baseline. comparisons has one entry for each variant other than the baseline, in name order. comparisons is empty and baseline is null when the experiment stores no baseline, and the figures of variants and metrics then keep their 95 percent ranges and no clear flag. Each comparison has variant, state, point (its goal value), cardsBehind (the cards behind its point: the finished cards for a rate, the delivered cards that have a value for any other metric), changeKind, change, holdReason, heldBy and guards. state is one of not-enough-cards, clear, not-clear or held. held means a control on the variant or on the baseline does not pass, so the comparison names no result, whatever the cards; holdReason is failed, unknown-metric or no-data, the first that any of those controls has in that order, and heldBy lists the metric keys of the controls with that result; both are null for any other state. A control on another variant holds no other comparison. not-enough-cards means the variant or the baseline has fewer than minFinishedCards cards behind its point. clear means the ranges of the variant and the baseline, at confidenceLevel, do not overlap. Otherwise state is not-clear. change is the change of the variant against the baseline, as point, low and high at confidenceLevel, or null when state is held or not-enough-cards, or the baseline point is zero. changeKind relative means change is a fraction of the baseline point, so -0.2 is 20 percent less. changeKind difference is for a goal of valueType ratio, and means change is the difference of the two ratios as a fraction between -1 and 1. A comparison guards entry has key, point (the variant value) and change, the variant minus the baseline as a range in the unit of the metric, or null when an arm has no data. For a ratio the change is a difference of ratios between -1 and 1. headline guards lists the metrics that the experiment must not worsen, each with key, label, valueType and baselinePoint. controls lists the checks that the treatment of a variant applied, each with metric (the key), variant, expect (a comparison and a number, such as "> 0", in the unit of the metric: dollars for a money value, milliseconds for a built-in duration, hours for a template duration), share (the share of cards with data that must meet it), passingShare (the share that do, or null when no card has data or the metric is unknown), cardsWithData, cardsFinished (the finished cards of the variant that the figures keep) and result. A card meets a control with the sum of the metric over its experiment runs. result is passed when passingShare reaches share, failed when it does not, no-data when no finished card has a value, and unknown-metric when the key is no metric of the project. Controls change no figure and leave no card out. Without a goal in the rule the goal is the cost, lower is better. The cost counts every worker run of the card, the covered cost counts the runs of the experiment of a covered kind, and the covered-cost key reads it as a goal, a guard or a metric. Without guards in the rule the guards are the merge rate and the fix rounds, when the template declares them. An empty guard list means no guards. Each variant has name, models (every model its experiment runs asked for, sorted), weight (null when the bridge sent none), cards and finishedCards (the kept cards, and those that merged or stand in a terminal column), runs (every worker run of the kept cards), costUsd (the cost of those runs) and coveredCostUsd (the cost of the runs of the experiment of a covered kind). Each cost is null when no kept card reported usage. Each metric has key, label (the name to show), valueType, clear, byVariant and parts. A metric that the workflow template declares has its own key and label. byVariant maps each variant to point, low and high, the value and its range at confidenceLevel, or to null when the variant has no data. clear is true when every variant other than the baseline is clear against the baseline: both have at least minFinishedCards cards behind their range, and their ranges do not overlap or their points are within 10 percent of the larger one. clear is false when any of those comparisons is not clear, and null when there is no baseline. A rate counts the finished cards, and a value per card counts the cards that ended with the delivered outcome of the template and have the value. A template with no delivered outcome gives no such cards. parts has the same shape, one row per value under a template count that splits by reason, role or kind, with the value type of its metric. includedCards and leftOutCards count the cards the figures keep and leave out. cards lists one page of cards, the latest run first, each with cardId, number, title, variant, column, runs (every worker run of the card), fixRounds, costUsd (every worker run), coveredCostUsd and leftOut. leftOut is empty for a kept card, else its reasons: switched (a run moved the card from a variant the rule no longer offers), mixed (its runs and its pin name more than one variant), before-test (a run with no experiment did a covered kind of work on the card first), covered-without-variant (a run with no experiment did a covered kind of work on the card at or after its first experiment run), no-history (the card history starts after its first experiment run) and no-run (a pin names the card and no experiment run worked it). Filter the cards with variant, which keeps the kept cards of one variant, or with leftOutOnly. The cards are paginated: pass page to walk further, and keep going while hasMore is true. total counts the cards that match the filters. An experiment with no run and no pin in this project is refused.

experiment.description: the name of the experiment, as worker_run_list and metric_query name it

page.description: the 1-based page of the cards to read

variant.description: only the kept cards of this variant

leftOutOnly.description: only the cards the figures leave out
